commit.message:
Make the scheduled lanes able to run at all

All four scheduled workflows had never executed once. Their crons fire on
Mondays and the repositories were created on a Wednesday, and workflow_dispatch
was enabled the whole time, so twenty-six of fifty-three job definitions had
simply never been observed. I dispatched three of them. Eleven jobs failed. Four
of the five hub failures are fixed here, each with its cause named.

Windows could not check the repository out. Not the lane: the checkout.

    error: invalid path 'fixtures/hostile/cases/nul.json'
    ##[error]The process 'git.exe' failed with exit code 128

`nul` is a reserved device name on Windows, so git cannot create that file and
every Windows claim this repository has ever made is about a checkout that never
happened. The fixture is renamed to nul-character.json, which is what it was
always about: a NUL character inside JSON, not a filename. Same bytes, same
CONTROL_CHARACTER_FORBIDDEN reason code, generator and consumer both updated.

macOS could not install Python. setup-python refused with "The version '3.12.12'
with architecture 'arm64' was not found for macOS 15.7.9". The exact patch was
never load-bearing: ops/ci/rust-toolchain-boundary.sh accepts any
^Python 3\.12\.[0-9]+$ and then verifies the resolved binary by digest. The pin
is now the 3.12 series, in the workflow and in the guard that asserts it, which
still stops a silent jump to 3.13 — the thing that guard is actually for.

Coverage never had a scanner. The coverage filter is the whole workspace, wider
than the fast lane's partition, so it reaches
publication::scan::tests::actual_pinned_scanner_detects_binary_and_chunk_boundary_canaries,
which admits the pinned scanner rather than skipping and therefore panicked at
src/publication/scan_tests.rs:130. The fast job already installs gitleaks for
exactly this reason; now the coverage job does too.

The links lane had never installed its own tool. taiki-e/install-action does not
carry lychee at the pinned revision and refused with "install-action does not
support lychee@0.24.0". ops/ci/install-lychee.sh replaces it in the same shape as
ops/ci/install-gitleaks.sh: one named asset over TLS, checked against the digest
upstream publishes beside it, refuse rather than continue. Verified locally
against the real documentation tree: 890 links, 889 OK, 0 errors.

The audit job is deliberately left failing. Exit 78 is not neutral in GitHub
Actions; it never was, and every "typed neutral refusal" written on that pattern
is a red job wearing a polite message. It cannot be repaired in the workflow
because ops/ci/artifact-check.sh requires an observation whose tool_versions
names jankurai, and there is no version to record when the tool is absent. That
is a contract four repositories share, so it is not mine to decide alone.
~/.bullet-orch-durable/CI-PORTABILITY-FINDINGS-20260910.md sets out three
options and my preference.

Six of the eight publication workflow digest pins are re-admitted from the
published mains, which clears PUBLICATION_CI_WORKFLOW_DIGEST_DRIFT. The topology
is unchanged; only bytes moved.
